question: Should crawl-remote deployments permanently retain this hidden Gitcrawl canary across Worker rollbacks and fail unless both predecessor and new runtimes expose exact query-level release provenance?
rationale: The patch deliberately creates a durable operational data contract and fail-closed rollout dependency whose retention and compatibility policy cannot be resolved by tests or mechanical repair.

options.title: Approve staged permanent canary
options.body: Land prerequisites first and accept permanent retention after a staged deploy-and-rollback proof confirms all six queries, listing exclusion, freshness, and exact release provenance.

options.title: Adopt an ephemeral canary
options.body: Revise the design around a release-scoped seed and cleanup process, avoiding permanent retained data but requiring a different rollback strategy.

options.title: Defer deployment enforcement
options.body: Keep the query evidence core separate until maintainers define long-term canary ownership, retention, and rollback policy.

recommendation.title: Approve staged permanent canary
recommendation.body: Land prerequisites first and accept permanent retention after a staged deploy-and-rollback proof confirms all six queries, listing exclusion, freshness, and exact release provenance.

likelyOwner.reason: This repository member owns the complete stacked implementation and is best positioned to present the intended rollout and operational contract for maintainer approval.
